passages.note: Clerk roll call 209: Houchin Yea on final passage of the Secure the Border Act, a bill spanning border barriers, asylum, parole, E-Verify, H-2A rules and DHS vaccine mandates.
passages.actor_quote: Houchin Houchin Republican Indiana IN Yea

passages.provision_quote: and has arrived in the United States at a port of entry
passages.note: Bill text: Div. B Title I limits asylum to port-of-entry arrivals and adds a transit bar (rung 4's clause), but the bill also carries many unrelated parts, so a Yea proves direction only absent her words tying the vote to this provision.
Her statement on H.R. 2 praises the bill as a whole ('strongest border bill') and names no asylum provision, so it does not tie the vote to rung 4's clause.
Criticizes the 2,500-per-day asylum suspension threshold as too weak and says 'Pass HR2'; shows the restrictive side but does not separate restricting asylum from ending it.

Press release reports an amicus brief backing Texas's state arrest law (state enforcement, not who may claim asylum); the brief itself is not in the snapshot, and her quoted words name no asylum clause.
Campaign issues page in third person (wall, law enforcement, deporting criminal aliens) is enforcement only and says nothing about asylum access.

rows.reasoning: Houchin voted Yea on H.R. 2 (118th), whose asylum title limits asylum to arrivals 'at a port of entry' and matches 'Sharply restrict who can claim asylum at the border', but the bill is multi-subject and her own statements praise it as a whole ('the strongest border bill in years', 'Pass HR2') without tying her vote to that provision. Her 2024 criticism of the 2,500-per-day suspension shows the restrictive side only and does not separate restricting asylum from 'End asylum and quickly turn back anyone who crosses illegally'.
